THE LAWS CONTINUED — CHAPTERS 18 THROUGH 26

DEVARIM — CHAPTER 18 The Levites' Due — A Prophet Like Me

18:1 The priests the Levites, even all the tribe of Levi, shall have no portion nor inheritance with Yisra'el; they shall eat the offerings of YHWH made by fire, and his inheritance.

18:2 And they shall have no inheritance among their brothers; YHWH is their inheritance, as he has spoken to them.

18:3 And this shall be the priests' due from the people, from them that offer a sacrifice, whether it be ox or sheep, that they shall give to the priest the shoulder, and the two cheeks, and the maw.

18:4 The first-fruits of your grain, of your wine, and of your oil, and the first of the fleece of your sheep, shall you give him.

18:5 For YHWH your Creator has chosen him out of all your tribes, to stand to minister in the name of YHWH, him and his sons for ever.

18:6 And if a Levite come from any of your gates out of all Yisra'el, where he sojourns, and come with all the desire of his soul to the place which YHWH shall choose;

18:7 then he shall minister in the name of YHWH his Creator, as all his brothers the Levites do, who stand there before YHWH.

18:8 They shall have equal portions to eat, besides that which is his due according to the fathers' houses.

18:9 When you have come into the land which YHWH your Creator gives you, you shall not learn to do after the abominations of those nations.

18:10 There shall not be found among you any one that makes his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, one that uses divination, a soothsayer, or an enchanter, or a sorcerer,

18:11 or a charmer, or one that consults a ghost or a familiar spirit, or a necromancer.

18:12 For whoever does these things is an abomination to YHWH; and because of these abominations YHWH your Creator is driving them out from before you.

18:13 You shall be whole-hearted with YHWH your Creator.

18:14 For these nations, that you are to dispossess, listen to soothsayers, and to diviners; but as for you, YHWH your Creator has not allowed you to do so.

18:15 A prophet will YHWH your Creator raise up for you, from your midst, of your brothers, like me; to him shall you listen;

18:16 according to all that you desired of YHWH your Creator at Chorev, on the day of the assembly, saying: Let me not hear again the voice of YHWH my Creator, neither let me see this great fire any more, that I die not.

18:17 And YHWH said to me: They have well said that which they have spoken.

18:18 I will raise them up a prophet from among their brothers, like you; and I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all that I shall command him.

18:19 And it shall come to pass, that whoever will not listen to my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him.

18:20 But the prophet, that shall speak a word presumptuously in my name, which I have not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, that same prophet shall die.

18:21 And if you say in your heart: How shall we know the word which YHWH has not spoken?

18:22 When a prophet speaks in the name of YHWH, if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, that is the thing which YHWH has not spoken; the prophet has spoken it presumptuously, you shall not be afraid of him.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing DSS census produces a confirmed reading specific to this chapter this session. Deuteronomy is among the most heavily attested books at Qumran overall (see Book-Level Critical Apparatus, Section 2), but no verse-level match for this chapter's specific content was confirmed from the secondary citations consulted this session.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verses 10-11 list eight distinct terms for forbidden divinatory and necromantic practice ("one that makes his son or daughter pass through the fire," a diviner, soothsayer, enchanter, sorcerer, charmer, one who consults a ghost or familiar spirit, and a necromancer); this reconstruction renders each term distinctly rather than collapsing near-synonyms, though the precise technical distinction between several of these Hebrew terms is not fully recoverable from context alone -- classification UNVERIFIED-OPEN for the exact practice each individually denotes. Verses 15 and 18's נביא כמני / כמוך ("a prophet like me / like you") establish a real, significant promise of prophetic succession "from among their brothers"; this reconstruction presents the promise exactly as this chapter states it, without importing later interpretive applications from outside this project's pre-Second-Temple, pre-Rabbinic, pre-Christian textual scope. Verses 21-22's criterion for distinguishing true from false prophecy (fulfillment or non-fulfillment of the spoken word) is preserved as the chapter's own stated test, without supplementing it with criteria drawn from elsewhere.

DEVARIM — CHAPTER 19 The Cities of Refuge — Witnesses — Life for Life

19:1 When YHWH your Creator shall cut off the nations, whose land YHWH your Creator gives you, and you succeed them, and dwell in their cities, and in their houses;

19:2 you shall separate three cities for yourself in the midst of your land, which YHWH your Creator gives you to possess it.

19:3 You shall prepare the way, and divide the borders of your land, which YHWH your Creator causes you to inherit, into three parts, that every manslayer may flee there.

19:4 And this is the case of the manslayer, that shall flee there and live: whoever kills his neighbor unawares, and hated him not in time past;

19:5 as when a man goes into the forest with his neighbor to cut wood, and his hand fetches a stroke with the axe to cut down the tree, and the head slips from the handle, and lights upon his neighbor, that he die; he shall flee to one of these cities and live;

19:6 lest the avenger of blood pursue the manslayer, while his heart is hot, and overtake him, because the way is long, and strike him mortally; whereas he was not deserving of death, since he hated him not in time past.

19:7 Wherefore I command you, saying: You shall separate three cities for yourself.

19:8 And if YHWH your Creator enlarge your border, as he has sworn to your fathers, and give you all the land which he promised to give to your fathers --

19:9 if you shall keep all this commandment to do it, which I command you this day, to love YHWH your Creator, and to walk ever in his ways -- then shall you add three cities more for yourself, besides these three;

19:10 that innocent blood be not shed in the midst of your land, which YHWH your Creator gives you for an inheritance, and so blood be upon you.

19:11 But if any man hate his neighbor, and lie in wait for him, and rise up against him, and strike him mortally that he die; and he flee into one of these cities;

19:12 then the elders of his city shall send and fetch him from there; and deliver him into the hand of the avenger of blood, that he may die.

19:13 Your eye shall not pity him, but you shall put away the blood of the innocent from Yisra'el, that it may go well with you.

19:14 You shall not remove your neighbor's landmark, which they of old time have set, in your inheritance which you shall inherit, in the land that YHWH your Creator gives you to possess it.

19:15 One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity, or for any sin, in any sin that he sins; at the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall a matter be established.

19:16 If an unrighteous witness rise up against any man to bear perverted witness against him;

19:17 then both the men, between whom the controversy is, shall stand before YHWH, before the priests and the judges that shall be in those days.

19:18 And the judges shall inquire diligently; and behold, if the witness be a false witness, and has testified falsely against his brother;

19:19 then shall you do to him, as he had purposed to do to his brother; so shall you put away the evil from your midst.

19:20 And those that remain shall hear, and fear, and shall henceforth commit no more any such evil in your midst.

19:21 And your eye shall not pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing DSS census produces a confirmed reading specific to this chapter this session. Deuteronomy is among the most heavily attested books at Qumran overall (see Book-Level Critical Apparatus, Section 2), but no verse-level match for this chapter's specific content was confirmed from the secondary citations consulted this session.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] A real, disclosed structural difference from the cities-of-refuge legislation already reconstructed at Bamidbar 35: this chapter frames the institution around three cities within the land (v.2), with a conditional provision for three additional cities should YHWH enlarge Yisra'el's border as sworn to the fathers (vv.8-9, for a possible total of six, or nine if counting the three already established east of the Yarden per Devarim 4:41-43), whereas Bamidbar 35:13-14 fixes the total at six cities from the outset (three east of the Yarden, three within Kena'an), without a conditional expansion mechanism. This reconstruction preserves each chapter's own framing without harmonizing the two into a single combined system. Verse 21's formula ("life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot") directly repeats the formula already reconstructed at Shemot 21:24 and Vayikra 24:20, rendered identically here in the specific context of perjury before a capital charge (vv.16-19).

DEVARIM — CHAPTER 20 Distant Cities and the Seven Nations — The Fruit Trees

20:1 When you go forth to battle against your enemies, and see horses, and chariots, and a people more than you, you shall not be afraid of them; for YHWH your Creator is with you, who brought you up out of the land of Mitzrayim.

20:2 And it shall be, when you draw near to the battle, that the priest shall approach and speak to the people,

20:3 and shall say to them: Hear, O Yisra'el, you draw near this day to battle against your enemies; let not your heart faint; fear not, nor be alarmed, neither be terrified at them;

20:4 for YHWH your Creator is he that goes with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.

20:5 And the officers shall speak to the people, saying: What man is there that has built a new house, and has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man dedicate it.

20:6 And what man is there that has planted a vineyard, and has not used its fruit? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man use its fruit.

20:7 And what man is there that has betrothed a wife, and has not taken her? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man take her.

20:8 And the officers shall speak further to the people, and they shall say: What man is there that is fearful and faint-hearted? Let him go and return to his house, lest his brothers' heart melt as his heart.

20:9 And it shall be, when the officers have made an end of speaking to the people, that captains of hosts shall be appointed at the head of the people.

20:10 When you draw near to a city to fight against it, then proclaim peace to it.

20:11 And it shall be, if it make you answer of peace, and open to you, then it shall be, that all the people that are found therein shall become tributary to you, and shall serve you.

20:12 And if it will make no peace with you, but will make war against you, then you shall besiege it.

20:13 And when YHWH your Creator delivers it into your hand, you shall strike every male thereof with the edge of the sword;

20:14 but the women, and the little ones, and the cattle, and all that is in the city, even all its spoil, shall you take for a prey to yourself; and you shall eat the spoil of your enemies, which YHWH your Creator has given you.

20:15 Thus shall you do to all the cities which are very far off from you, which are not of the cities of these nations.

20:16 Howbeit of the cities of these peoples, that YHWH your Creator gives you for an inheritance, you shall save alive nothing that breathes,

20:17 but you shall utterly destroy them: the Chiti, and the Emori, the Kena'ani, and the Perizi, the Chivi, and the Yevusi; as YHWH your Creator has commanded you;

20:18 that they teach you not to do after all their abominations, which they have done to their gods, and so you sin against YHWH your Creator.

20:19 When you shall besiege a city a long time, in making war against it to take it, you shall not destroy its trees by wielding an axe against them; for you may eat of them, but you shall not cut them down; for is the tree of the field man, that it should be besieged by you?

20:20 Only the trees of which you know that they are not trees for food, them you may destroy and cut down, that you may build siegeworks against the city that makes war with you, until it fall.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing DSS census produces a confirmed reading specific to this chapter this session. Deuteronomy is among the most heavily attested books at Qumran overall (see Book-Level Critical Apparatus, Section 2), but no verse-level match for this chapter's specific content was confirmed from the secondary citations consulted this session.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] This chapter draws an explicit two-tiered distinction preserved without harmonization: for cities "very far off" (v.15), peace is offered first, and only males are killed if war follows (vv.10-15); for the cities of the named peoples given as an inheritance (the same seven nations already listed at 7:1), no peace is offered and nothing that breathes is spared (vv.16-18), with the chapter's own stated rationale being to prevent their abominations from being taught (v.18) -- a rationale this reconstruction presents exactly as given, without independent ethical commentary. Verses 19-20's provision protecting fruit-bearing trees from destruction during a siege is a real, distinctive law with no direct parallel elsewhere in the Torah as reconstructed in this project; this reconstruction preserves the rhetorical question ("is the tree of the field man, that it should be besieged by you?") exactly as MT poses it.

DEVARIM — CHAPTER 21 The Unsolved Slaying — The Captive Woman — The Rebellious Son

21:1 If one be found slain in the land which YHWH your Creator gives you to possess it, lying in the field, and it be not known who has struck him;

21:2 then your elders and your judges shall come forth, and they shall measure to the cities which are round about him that is slain.

21:3 And it shall be, that the city which is nearest to the slain man, even the elders of that city shall take a heifer of the herd, which has not been worked with, and which has not drawn in the yoke.

21:4 And the elders of that city shall bring down the heifer to a rough valley, which may neither be plowed nor sown, and shall break the heifer's neck there in the valley.

21:5 And the priests the sons of Levi shall come near -- for them YHWH your Creator has chosen to minister to him, and to bless in the name of YHWH; and according to their word shall every controversy and every stroke be.

21:6 And all the elders of that city, who are nearest to the slain man, shall wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the valley.

21:7 And they shall speak and say: Our hands have not shed this blood, neither have our eyes seen it.

21:8 Forgive, O YHWH, your people Yisra'el, whom you have redeemed, and do not let innocent blood remain in the midst of your people Yisra'el. And the blood shall be forgiven them.

21:9 So shall you put away the innocent blood from your midst, when you shall do that which is right in the eyes of YHWH.

21:10 When you go forth to battle against your enemies, and YHWH your Creator delivers them into your hands, and you carry them away captive,

21:11 and see among the captives a woman of goodly form, and you have a desire to her, and would take her to yourself as wife;

21:12 then you shall bring her home to your house; and she shall shave her head, and pare her nails;

21:13 and she shall put the garment of her captivity from off her, and shall remain in your house, and mourn her father and her mother a full month; and after that you may go in to her, and be her husband, and she shall be your wife.

21:14 And it shall be, if you have no delight in her, then you shall let her go where she will; but you shall not sell her at all for money, you shall not deal with her as a slave, because you have humbled her.

21:15 If a man have two wives, the one beloved, and the other hated, and they have borne him children, both the beloved and the hated; and if the firstborn son be hers that was hated;

21:16 then it shall be, in the day that he causes his sons to inherit that which he has, that he may not make the son of the beloved the firstborn before the son of the hated, who is the firstborn;

21:17 but he shall acknowledge the firstborn, the son of the hated, by giving him a double portion of all that he has; for he is the first-fruits of his strength, the right of the firstborn is his.

21:18 If a man have a stubborn and rebellious son, that will not listen to the voice of his father, or the voice of his mother, and though they chasten him, will not listen to them;

21:19 then shall his father and his mother lay hold on him, and bring him out to the elders of his city, and to the gate of his place;

21:20 and they shall say to the elders of his city: This our son is stubborn and rebellious, he does not listen to our voice; he is a glutton, and a drunkard.

21:21 And all the men of his city shall stone him with stones, that he die; so shall you put away the evil from your midst; and all Yisra'el shall hear, and fear.

21:22 And if a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and he be put to death, and you hang him on a tree;

21:23 his body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but you shall surely bury him the same day; for he that is hanged is a reproach to the Creator; that you defile not your land which YHWH your Creator gives you for an inheritance.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing DSS census produces a confirmed reading specific to this chapter this session. Deuteronomy is among the most heavily attested books at Qumran overall (see Book-Level Critical Apparatus, Section 2), but no verse-level match for this chapter's specific content was confirmed from the secondary citations consulted this session.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] This chapter presents four distinct, juxtaposed cases (unsolved slaying, vv.1-9; a captive woman taken as wife, vv.10-14; inheritance rights between a beloved and a hated wife's sons, vv.15-17; a stubborn and rebellious son, vv.18-21) with a closing provision on burial of the executed (vv.22-23); this reconstruction preserves the juxtaposition exactly as MT places it, without supplying a unifying rationale MT itself does not state. Verse 23's קללת אלהים is rendered "a reproach to the Creator," consistent with this project's treatment of generic references to the deity; MT's own reasoning for the same-day burial requirement (avoiding land defilement) is preserved without importing later reception of this verse from outside this project's textual scope. Verse 14's provision that a captive wife who is not desired must be released, never sold or treated as property, is preserved as this chapter's own stated restriction on an otherwise disclosed practice, without independent ethical commentary on the practice itself.

DEVARIM — CHAPTER 22 Lost Property — Mixed Kinds — Tzitzit — Virginity Law

22:1 You shall not see your brother's ox or his sheep driven away, and hide yourself from them: you shall surely bring them back to your brother.

22:2 And if your brother be not near to you, and you know him not, then you shall bring it home to your house, and it shall be with you until your brother requires it, and you shall restore it to him.

22:3 And so shall you do with his donkey; and so shall you do with his garment; and so shall you do with every lost thing of your brother's, which he has lost, and you have found: you may not hide yourself.

22:4 You shall not see your brother's donkey or his ox fallen down by the way, and hide yourself from them: you shall surely help him to lift them up again.

22:5 A woman shall not wear that which pertains to a man, neither shall a man put on a woman's garment; for whoever does these things is an abomination to YHWH your Creator.

22:6 If a bird's nest chance to be before you in the way, in any tree or on the ground, with young ones or eggs, and the mother sitting upon the young, or upon the eggs, you shall not take the mother with the young;

22:7 you shall in any wise let the mother go, but the young you may take for yourself; that it may be well with you, and that you may prolong your days.

22:8 When you build a new house, then you shall make a parapet for your roof, that you bring not blood upon your house, if any man fall from there.

22:9 You shall not sow your vineyard with two kinds of seed; lest the fullness of the seed which you have sown be forfeited together with the increase of the vineyard.

22:10 You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together.

22:11 You shall not wear a mingled fabric, wool and linen together.

22:12 You shall make for yourself twisted cords upon the four corners of your covering, with which you cover yourself.

22:13 If any man take a wife, and go in to her, and hate her,

22:14 and lay wanton charges against her, and bring up an evil name upon her, and say: I took this woman, and when I came near to her, I did not find in her the tokens of virginity;

22:15 then shall the father of the young woman, and her mother, take and bring forth the tokens of the young woman's virginity to the elders of the city at the gate.

22:16 And the young woman's father shall say to the elders: I gave my daughter to this man as wife, and he hates her;

22:17 and behold, he has laid wanton charges, saying: I did not find in your daughter the tokens of virginity; and yet these are the tokens of my daughter's virginity. And they shall spread the garment before the elders of the city.

22:18 And the elders of that city shall take the man and chastise him.

22:19 And they shall fine him a hundred shekels of silver, and give them to the father of the young woman, because he has brought up an evil name upon a virgin of Yisra'el; and she shall be his wife; he may not put her away all his days.

22:20 But if this thing be true, that the tokens of virginity were not found in the young woman;

22:21 then they shall bring out the young woman to the door of her father's house, and the men of her city shall stone her with stones that she die; because she has wrought a wanton deed in Yisra'el, to play the harlot in her father's house; so shall you put away the evil from your midst.

22:22 If a man be found lying with a woman married to a husband, then they shall both of them die, the man that lay with the woman, and the woman; so shall you put away the evil from Yisra'el.

22:23 If there be a young woman that is a virgin betrothed to a man, and a man find her in the city, and lie with her;

22:24 then you shall bring them both out to the gate of that city, and you shall stone them with stones that they die: the young woman, because she cried not, being in the city; and the man, because he has humbled his neighbor's wife; so you shall put away the evil from your midst.

22:25 But if the man find the betrothed young woman in the field, and the man take hold of her, and lie with her; then the man only that lay with her shall die.

22:26 But to the young woman you shall do nothing; there is in the young woman no sin worthy of death: for as when a man rises against his neighbor, and slays him, even so is this matter.

22:27 For he found her in the field; the betrothed young woman cried, and there was none to save her.

22:28 If a man find a young woman that is a virgin, that is not betrothed, and lay hold on her, and lie with her, and they be found;

22:29 then the man that lay with her shall give to the young woman's father fifty shekels of silver, and she shall be his wife, because he has humbled her; he may not put her away all his days.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing DSS census produces a confirmed reading specific to this chapter this session. Deuteronomy is among the most heavily attested books at Qumran overall (see Book-Level Critical Apparatus, Section 2), but no verse-level match for this chapter's specific content was confirmed from the secondary citations consulted this session.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] A real, confirmed Hebrew/English chapter-boundary offset, directly parallel to those already documented in this project (Bamidbar 16/17, 29/30; Devarim 13): this chapter's 29 verses under Hebrew/Mechon-Mamre numbering (followed here per the ACR's own MT/UXLC-based standard) correspond to 30 verses under common English versification, with English's additional final verse (concerning a man and his father's wife) numbered as the opening of Deuteronomy 23 in that convention. This reconstruction's numbering is used consistently; no textual content differs between the two systems, only the placement of the chapter boundary.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 12's instruction to make twisted cords (גדלים) on the four corners of one's covering directly parallels the tzitzit legislation already reconstructed at Bamidbar 15:37-41, though this verse gives substantially less detail (no mention of the blue thread specified at Bamidbar 15:38); this reconstruction presents this chapter's brief instruction without importing the fuller Bamidbar specification into it. Verses 13-21's procedure for contested virginity claims and verses 23-27's distinction between an assault occurring in a city (where an unheard cry is treated as consent) versus in a field (where the woman is presumed to have cried for help unheard) are preserved exactly as MT presents them, without softening or ethical commentary; this reconstruction discloses these as genuine, disclosed features of the legal text rather than omitting or reframing them.

DEVARIM — CHAPTER 23 The Assembly of YHWH — Camp Purity — Vows — Gleaning

23:1 A man shall not take his father's wife, and shall not uncover his father's skirt.

23:2 He that is crushed or maimed in his privy parts shall not enter into the assembly of YHWH.

23:3 A bastard shall not enter into the assembly of YHWH; even to the tenth generation shall none of his enter into the assembly of YHWH.

23:4 An Ammonite or a Moabite shall not enter into the assembly of YHWH; even to the tenth generation shall none of them enter into the assembly of YHWH for ever;

23:5 because they did not meet you with bread and with water in the way, when you came forth out of Mitzrayim; and because they hired against you Bil'am the son of Be'or from Petor of Aram-Naharayim, to curse you.

23:6 Nevertheless YHWH your Creator would not listen to Bil'am; but YHWH your Creator turned the curse into a blessing for you, because YHWH your Creator loved you.

23:7 You shall not seek their peace nor their prosperity all your days for ever.

23:8 You shall not abhor an Edomite, for he is your brother; you shall not abhor an Egyptian, because you were a stranger in his land.

23:9 The children of the third generation that are born to them may enter into the assembly of YHWH.

23:10 When you go forth in camp against your enemies, then you shall keep yourself from every evil thing.

23:11 If there be among you any man, that is not clean by reason of that which happens to him by night, then shall he go outside the camp, he shall not come within the camp.

23:12 But it shall be, when evening comes on, he shall bathe himself in water; and when the sun is down, he may come within the camp.

23:13 You shall have a place also outside the camp, where you shall go forth.

23:14 And you shall have a paddle among your weapons; and it shall be, when you sit down outside, you shall dig with it, and shall turn back and cover that which comes from you.

23:15 For YHWH your Creator walks in the midst of your camp, to deliver you, and to give up your enemies before you; therefore shall your camp be holy; that he see no unseemly thing in you, and turn away from you.

23:16 You shall not deliver to his master a bondman that has escaped from his master to you;

23:17 he shall dwell with you, in your midst, in the place which he shall choose within one of your gates, where it pleases him best; you shall not wrong him.

23:18 There shall be no harlot of the daughters of Yisra'el, neither shall there be a sodomite of the sons of Yisra'el.

23:19 You shall not bring the hire of a harlot, or the price of a dog, into the house of YHWH your Creator for any vow; for even both these are an abomination to YHWH your Creator.

23:20 You shall not lend upon interest to your brother: interest of money, interest of food, interest of anything that is lent upon interest.

23:21 To a foreigner you may lend upon interest; but to your brother you shall not lend upon interest; that YHWH your Creator may bless you in all that you put your hand to, in the land where you go in to possess it.

23:22 When you shall vow a vow to YHWH your Creator, you shall not be slack to pay it; for YHWH your Creator will surely require it of you; and it will be sin in you.

23:23 But if you shall forbear to vow, it shall be no sin in you.

23:24 That which has gone out of your lips you shall observe and do; according as you have vowed freely to YHWH your Creator, even that which you have promised with your mouth.

23:25 When you come into your neighbor's vineyard, then you may eat grapes until you have enough at your own pleasure; but you shall not put any in your vessel.

23:26 When you come into your neighbor's standing grain, then you may pluck ears with your hand; but you shall not move a sickle to your neighbor's standing grain.

This reconstruction adopts the majority reading in translation while disclosing the grammatical basis for the minority reading rather than treating it as settled beyond dispute. 33:3 Yes, he loves the peoples, all his holy ones are in your hand; and they sit down at your feet, receiving of your words.

33:4 Moshe commanded us a law, an inheritance of the congregation of Ya'akov.

33:5 And there was a king in Yeshurun, when the heads of the people were gathered, all the tribes of Yisra'el together.

33:6 Let Re'uven live, and not die, in that his men become few.

33:7 And this for Yehudah, and he said: Hear, YHWH, the voice of Yehudah, and bring him in to his people; his hands shall contend for him, and you shall be a help against his adversaries.

33:8 And of Levi he said: Your Tumim and your Urim be with your holy one, whom you proved at Massah, with whom you strove at the waters of Merivah;

33:9 who said of his father, and of his mother: I have not seen him; neither did he acknowledge his brothers, nor knew he his own children: for they have observed your word, and keep your covenant.

33:10 They shall teach Ya'akov your ordinances, and Yisra'el your law: they shall put incense before you, and whole burnt-offering upon your altar.

33:11 Bless, YHWH, his substance, and accept the work of his hands: strike through the loins of them that rise up against him, and of them that hate him, that they rise not again.

33:12 Of Binyamin he said: The beloved of YHWH shall dwell in safety by him; he covers him all the day, and he dwells between his shoulders.

33:13 And of Yosef he said: Blessed of YHWH be his land; for the precious things of heaven, for the dew, and for the deep that lies beneath,

33:14 and for the precious things of the fruits of the sun, and for the precious things of the yield of the moons,

33:15 and for the tops of the ancient mountains, and for the precious things of the everlasting hills,

33:16 and for the precious things of the earth and its fullness, and the good will of him that dwelt in the bush: let the blessing come upon the head of Yosef, and upon the crown of the head of him that is prince among his brothers.

33:17 His firstling bullock, majesty is his; and his horns are the horns of the wild-ox: with them he shall gore the peoples all of them, even the ends of the earth; and they are the ten thousands of Efrayim, and they are the thousands of Menashe.

33:18 And of Zevulun he said: Rejoice, Zevulun, in your going out, and, Yissakhar, in your tents.

33:19 They shall call peoples to the mountain; there shall they offer sacrifices of righteousness: for they shall suck the abundance of the seas, and the hidden treasures of the sand.

33:20 And of Gad he said: Blessed be he that enlarges Gad: he dwells as a lioness, and tears the arm, even the crown of the head.

33:21 And he chose a first part for himself, for there a portion of a ruler was reserved; and there came the heads of the people, he executed the righteousness of YHWH, and his ordinances with Yisra'el.

33:22 And of Dan he said: Dan is a lion's cub, that leaps forth from Bashan.

33:23 And of Naftali he said: O Naftali, satisfied with favor, and full with the blessing of YHWH: possess the sea and the south.

33:24 And of Asher he said: Blessed be Asher above sons; let him be the favored of his brothers, and let him dip his foot in oil.

33:25 Iron and brass shall be your bars; and as your days, so shall your strength be.

33:26 There is none like the Creator, O Yeshurun, who rides upon the heaven as your help, and in his excellency on the skies.

33:27 The eternal Creator is a dwelling-place, and underneath are the everlasting arms: and he thrust out the enemy from before you, and said: Destroy.

33:28 And Yisra'el dwells in safety, the fountain of Ya'akov alone, in a land of grain and wine; yes, his heavens drop down dew.

33:29 Happy are you, O Yisra'el, who is like you? A people saved by YHWH, the shield of your help, and that is the sword of your excellency! And your enemies shall dwindle away before you; and you shall tread upon their high places.

DEVARIM — CHAPTER 34 There Has Not Arisen a Prophet Since

34:1 And Moshe went up from the plains of Mo'av to mount Nevo, to the top of Pisgah, that is opposite Yericho. And YHWH showed him all the land, even Gil'ad as far as Dan;

34:2 and all Naftali, and the land of Efrayim and Menashe, and all the land of Yehudah as far as the hinder sea;

34:3 and the South, and the Plain, even the valley of Yericho the city of palm trees, as far as Tzo'ar.

34:4 And YHWH said to him: This is the land which I swore to Avraham, to Yitzhak, and to Ya'akov, saying: I will give it to your seed; I have caused you to see it with your eyes, but you shall not go over there.

34:5 So Moshe the servant of YHWH died there in the land of Mo'av, according to the word of YHWH.

34:6 And he was buried in the valley in the land of Mo'av over against Beit-Pe'or; and no man knows his burial place to this day.

34:7 And Moshe was a hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.

34:8 And the children of Yisra'el wept for Moshe in the plains of Mo'av thirty days; so the days of weeping in the mourning for Moshe were ended.

34:9 And Yehoshu'a the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moshe had laid his hands upon him; and the children of Yisra'el listened to him, and did as YHWH commanded Moshe.

34:10 And there has not arisen a prophet since in Yisra'el like Moshe, whom YHWH knew face to face;

34:11 in all the signs and the wonders, which YHWH sent him to do in the land of Mitzrayim, to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to all his land;

34:12 and in all the mighty hand, and in all the great terror, which Moshe wrought in the sight of all Yisra'el.
